solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In which to wrap cold fish skin?

parts.note: C = cold, as on a tap
the ling is a fish of the cod family
a film is a thin skin, as on custard

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what to wrap a chilled piece of fish skin in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description: you really would wrap cold fish in clingfilm, which is the British name for plastic food wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Clingfilm is the thin plastic sheet food is wrapped in.

clue.text: Copper penny placed on the Spanish assayer's bowl

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first pieces sit on top of what follows

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a copper coin on a Spanish assayer's dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive belongs to the definition, not to 'the Spanish': the Spanish article just supplies EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupel is the small porous dish in which an assayer tests precious metals.

clue.text: Moving slowly, using hoist when shipping whiskey

indicators.note: to ship something can mean to lose or shed it

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO alphabet; it is removed

explanation.surface: Cargo creeps upward as a winch lifts crates of whiskey aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipping' looks like loading cargo, which suits the hoist; here it means losing, as a boat ships oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Inching is moving forward by tiny amounts.

clue.text: Roughly, fiver ought to cover Charlie's prezzie?

indicators.note: roughly = not in exact order, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone reckons a five-pound note should just about pay for Charlie's present.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Charlie is 'is', joining wordplay to definition. A prezzie is British slang for a present; the question mark flags that a voucher is only one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift voucher is a present that can be exchanged for goods.

clue.text: Provoke enlightenment when giving speech

indicators.note: speech means the word is heard, not read

explanation.surface: A speaker rouses the crowd by sharing a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a rousing orator, so 'Provoke' and 'speech' seem to belong together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to provoke a riot and to incite one both mean stirring people into action.

clue.text: Wizard chap entertaining US soldier and spies

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them inside

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: A wizard hosts a GI and some secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' reads as a performer amusing an audience, which suits a wizard; it means holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both a wizard and a magician work magic, whether in legend or on stage.

clue.text: Raw meat changing hands

parts.note: the L of FLESH becomes R

explanation.surface: Uncooked meat is sold on to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' looks like a sale; in crosswords L and R stand for left and right, so the hands here are letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh and raw both describe food not yet cooked or processed.

clue.text: Charge iron-clad terminal of electrode

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the terminal is the end, the last letter

explanation.surface: An electrical terminal gets an iron casing, with a nod to a battery's charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical words make 'Charge' look like current; it is a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the money sense: what a lawyer charges is their fee.

clue.text: For the select few, English literature is translated into German

indicators.note: the word 'is' is given in German, where it is ist

parts.note: lit = literature, as in Eng Lit

explanation.surface: A remark that English literature in German translation is only for a small elite.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word 'is' is translated, not the literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elitist is aimed at a privileged few.

clue.text: Holiday cash antipodean yob received from Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: money = cash; it hands its M to the next word and takes that word's H
hoon = Australian yob; it takes the M and gives up its H

explanation.surface: A holiday funded by money taken from an Australian lout.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoon is Australian and New Zealand slang for a loutish young man. Swap the M and H of MONEY HOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the trip newlyweds take after the wedding is one particular holiday.

clue.text: A lot of water gathering in cheap AC if I connect

indicators.note: the answer is gathered inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Water pools in a cheap air-conditioning unit once it is plugged in.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised AC, suggesting air conditioning, is just letters in the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific is the largest ocean, a great deal of water.

clue.text: Classical scholar — shocking ignorance? No, no!

indicators.note: shocking = disordered, so the letters are mixed
read as 'no NO': take the letters N and O out

explanation.surface: An outraged reaction to a classicist's appalling lack of knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, no!' looks like horror at the ignorance; it is an instruction to drop NO.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense: someone versed in ancient Greek language and literature was once called by this name.

clue.text: One ceremonially necked sloe gin periodically

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter

explanation.surface: Someone ceremonially knocks back sloe gin every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Necked' is slang for drinking in one go, which fits the gin; here it means worn round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian flower garland hung round the neck in welcome.

clue.text: See the country in its entirety?

definitions.text: See the country in its entirety?

parts.note: not the verb but a see, a bishop's seat; the Holy See is the Pope's
the Holy See's territory is a whole sovereign state, and a tiny one

explanation.surface: A tourist invitation to tour a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a verb but the Holy See, the Pope's seat, and that see makes up the whole of its tiny country.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City, the seat of the Holy See, is an entire sovereign state.

clue.text: Fiddle, perhaps, a recurrent problem for seer

parts.note: a mere fiddle is no Strad, not a Stradivarius violin
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A fraud that keeps coming back to trouble a fortune-teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a swindle, which suits a dodgy seer; it is a violin, and an ordinary one is 'no Strad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostradamus was the French astrologer famed for his prophecies.

clue.text: Meaty dish leads to really agonising joint pain

indicators.note: the leads of words are the letters that go in front, their first letters

parts.note: gout is a painful swelling of the joints

explanation.surface: Rich meaty food brings on a bout of agonising gout.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair piece of medical folk wisdom: rich meat is blamed for gout.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a rich meat stew.

clue.text: Bloody cut of beef as well as symbol of order

parts.note: rib is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: A rare rib of beef, served alongside a mark of good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as tidiness; it is an order of knighthood, the Order of the Bath, whose emblem is the red riband.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the ribbon worn by members of the Order of the Bath marks their membership.

clue.text: Challengingly pitched battle on river

indicators.note: in an across clue, the battle comes on after the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A pitched battle is fought beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitched battle' is a stock phrase, but 'pitched' belongs to the definition, about the pitch of a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto describes singing pitched unnaturally high, a strain for a male voice.

clue.text: Plant acorn I've cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A gardener boasts of the oak seedling they have grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb telling you to sow the acorn; it is the noun, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: speedwell, with its small blue flowers, belongs to this genus.

clue.text: Girl embarrassed over admitting anything

explanation.surface: A girl blushes before owning up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: DER is split to take AUGHT inside: D-AUGHT-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a girl, as someone's female child.

clue.text: Angry, in an excited state and tense

parts.note: up = excited, as in 'all het up'

explanation.surface: A description of someone cross, wound up and on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a list of three synonyms for one mood; only the first word is the definition, and the other two are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight can mean irritated or angry as well as anxious.

clue.text: At sea, giant recovery vessel brought back toy boy

parts.note: Noah's ark saved the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A salvage ship at sea brings a young lover home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' means a much younger lover; here it is a boy who is literally a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The kraken is a giant sea monster of Norse legend.

clue.text: Army recruiter leaving the old Queen room

indicators.note: the old Queen's letters leave the name

parts.note: Lord Kitchener fronted the 'Your country needs you' recruiting poster

explanation.surface: A recruiting officer leaves the late Queen's chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener was Britain's War Secretary in 1914, pointing out from the famous recruitment poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the kitchen is one of the rooms of a house.

clue.text: Spare agent takes on work by Kipling

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Kim is Kipling's novel about a boy spy in India

explanation.surface: A reserve agent is handed a Kipling assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like a spare agent, a backup; it is the adjective meaning meagre.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare and skimpy both mean scanty or meagre.

clue.text: Italian team secured; could Spurs be like this?

parts.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club

explanation.surface: A football report: the Italian side has won, and Tottenham might be tied up the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; lower-case spurs, like a cockerel's or a rider's, could get interlocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlocked means locked together, as tangled spurs might be.

clue.text: Best toy

definitions.meaning: an adjective for first-rate, as in the marks at the head of the class
a child's toy that spins on its point when whipped or twirled

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, each a definition on its own; the pair reads like a shop label.
explanation.definitionFit: Top means best, and a top is a child's spinning toy.

clue.text: Adolescent infatuation over a Turkish title

parts.note: a pash is British schoolgirl slang for a crush

explanation.surface: A teenager's crush on an Ottoman dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: PASH is dated British slang, short for passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasha was a title given to high officials in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Fagin criminally acquiring hard American currency

indicators.note: a crime twists things, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Dickens's thieving Fagin gets his hands on hard dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard American currency' reads as dollars; only 'currency' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Afghanistan's money is one of the world's currencies.

clue.text: Mad after uncovering weapon

indicators.note: taking the cover off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: barmy = mad; B and Y removed

explanation.surface: A madman goes looking for a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is the link: the wordplay comes after uncovering, giving the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly plural: arms are weapons, as in an arms dealer or a firearm.

clue.text: Mass stress evacuating a small city

indicators.note: emptying out, so A and S leave

parts.note: A and S (small) are taken out of EMPHASIS

explanation.surface: Mass anxiety empties a little town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small city' looks like the definition; 'small' is S, and the city is a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: Memphis is a city in Tennessee and was a capital of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Bit of info okay for Russian corporation

parts.note: a corporation is jokey old slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A business snippet: approval is given for a Russian firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company; in dated British slang it is a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information.

clue.text: Train Issy Bailey, back to entertain old country

indicators.note: the answer runs backwards
the clue words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: trAIN ISSY BAiley, read right to left

explanation.surface: A coach tells someone called Issy Bailey to come back and host a former nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd names are there only to hold the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A former name: Ethiopia was known to Europeans by this name until the mid-twentieth century.
